title: SDKs: standardize route tagging (request option + header) across Python/TS (+Go follow-up)
creator: Monica Patel
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Goal
- Enable customers to attribute cost/latency to developer-defined "routes" in Usage Insights.
- Provide a consistent way to set route identifiers across SDKs without breaking existing integrations.
- Ensure route tagging works for streaming and non-streaming calls and is easy to adopt (minimal code changes).

Background
Usage Insights introduces a new telemetry dimension: `route`. The telemetry pipeline will ingest this from either:
1) an SDK-provided identifier (preferred, explicit)
2) gateway-derived route (fallback)

This ticket covers the SDK side: adding/standardizing a route tagging helper or standardized header emission.

Proposal (API surface)
- Standard header name: `X-Redwood-Route`
  - Value: developer-supplied route identifier (string)
  - Scope: per request; optional
  - Server-side will apply canonicalization/normalization per ADR; client should not attempt to be "too smart".

SDK ergonomics (consistent across languages)
1) Per-request option
- TypeScript: `client.responses.create({ ..., route: "chat.completions" })` (exact call shape depends on current SDK)
- Python: `client.responses.create(..., route="chat.completions")`
- Go (follow-up if time allows in this cycle): `Route: redwood.String("chat.completions")` or functional option `WithRoute("...")`

2) Global default (nice-to-have, not required for GA)
- Allow setting a default route prefix at client construction (e.g., `route_prefix="api"`) to reduce repetition. If we can’t ship safely without churn, skip for GA.

Naming guidance (should match docs/standards)
- Recommend stable, low-cardinality, human-readable identifiers.
- Examples: `auth.login`, `support.rerank`, `docqa.answer`, `agent.run`
- Explicitly discourage including user IDs, session IDs, UUIDs, or raw URLs.

Constraints / non-goals
- Do not introduce breaking changes to existing request option objects.
- Do not rename existing request fields unless we provide backwards-compat aliases.
- Do not attempt to enforce cardinality budgets in the SDK (server will guard). We can optionally add a warning/log in debug mode if route is extremely long.

Implementation plan
A) TypeScript SDK
- Add optional `route?: string` to the shared request options type (the object that all endpoints accept).
- Ensure `route` is mapped to `X-Redwood-Route` header.
- Confirm it’s included on streaming requests as well.
- Tests:
  - unit test that `route` becomes `X-Redwood-Route` header
  - streaming test (mock server) verifies header is present on the initial request
  - regression test: no `route` => header not set

B) Python SDK
- Add optional `route: Optional[str] = None` to relevant high-level methods (Responses/Chat/Embeddings depending on the SDK structure).
- Ensure `route` is passed through for both sync and streaming clients.
- Tests:
  - unit test on request builder that header is included
  - streaming generator test ensures header emitted

C) Docs/DevEx hooks
- Provide minimal snippet(s) for SDK README/docstrings to unblock ENG-8431 (Docs).
- Confirm examples align with the Console route breakdown (same string appears in UI).

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TS SDK: callers can pass `route` per request; SDK sends `X-Redwood-Route`.
- [ ] Python SDK: callers can pass `route` per request; SDK sends `X-Redwood-Route`.
- [ ] Streaming: route header included for streaming and non-streaming.
- [ ] Tests in each SDK cover header emission and default behavior.
- [ ] Example snippet ready for docs (ENG-8431) and quickstart update (ENG-8432 should link but not block).

Open questions
1) Exact header casing
- Suggest `X-Redwood-Route` (canonical). HTTP is case-insensitive, but we should standardize for debugging.

2) Field name: `route` vs `route_id`
- Preference: `route` (short, matches UI and telemetry dimension name).

3) Back-compat / collisions
- Verify no existing option named `route` in TS/Python SDKs.

References
- Confluence ADR: route dimension definition & normalization (canonicalization handled server-side)
- Linear: ENG-8421 (telemetry pipeline emits/ingests route)
- Linear: ENG-8431 (docs updates depend on stable SDK API)

Tracking
- TypeScript PR: github/redwood-sdk-typescript (target: PR-233)
- Python PR: github/redwood-sdk-python (target: PR-417)

Risks
- Inconsistent endpoint coverage: some SDKs expose multiple entry points (chat/responses). Ensure we add `route` in the shared request options layer.
- Streaming code path divergence (especially in Python): ensure header injection happens at the same layer as auth headers.
- Customers may assume raw URLs are acceptable: docs need to call out cardinality best practices explicitly.
comments: 2026-02-07 (Monica Patel): Creating this to lock in the SDK API surface before Docs starts screenshots/snippets. Proposed `route` param -> `X-Redwood-Route`. Please flag if any existing SDK option conflicts.

2026-02-10 (Alex Martinez): +1 on `route` naming. Please avoid adding any automatic URL-to-route mapping in SDKs; we want customers to choose stable names. Docs will carry the best-practices guidance.

2026-02-11 (Nadia Rahman): Server normalization will handle trimming/character constraints. If you can, add a lightweight client-side guard: if route > 200 chars, drop + log (debug) rather than sending huge header values.

2026-02-14 (Wei Chen): For docs, we need one minimal snippet per language and one "framework-ish" snippet (FastAPI/Express) showing where to set it. Please put examples in docstrings/README so we can link directly.

2026-02-18 (Monica Patel): TS implementation in progress: added `route?: string` to request options type and mapped to `X-Redwood-Route`. Next: streaming path + tests. Python queued after TS lands to keep behavior consistent.

2026-02-22 (Allison Grant): Please confirm route header is present on retries as well (same request options reused). This matters for attribution if there’s transient capacity fallback causing retries.
